text.p: - Russia's government wants to stop people drawing pensions after they retire if they continue to earn extra money.
- The opposition's threat to call a vote of no-confidence in the government appears aimed at forcing early parliamentary elections.
- Central Bank chairman Sergei Dubinin predicts growth of money supply will exceed price growth by 22-30 percent next year.
- Russia is likely to receive the next tranche of its IMF loan by the end of December or beginning of January next year.
- The Kremlin is obviously not interested in changing its policy in Chechnya till January 27 elections in the region.
- The government will have to subsidise key industries to the tune of $170-190 billion to keep economic reforms on track, economy minister Yevgeny Yasin is quoted as saying.
- The government's debt to pensioners is worth 17 trillion roubles and might reach 20 trillion by January 1997.

- Omsk, a big industrial center in Siberia, has become the third Russian city (after St.Petersburg and Irkutsk) to set up a vice squad. It is also the only region where a law on regulating the distribution of erotic materials has been working for the last two years.
- The Duma is expected to discuss the legality of President Yeltsin's recent actions but has no grounds for impeaching him.
- Alexander Korzhakov, Yeltsin's sacked bodyguard, used to interview people before they could work for the president, says Sergei Medvedev, Yeltsin's former press secretary.
